NOTES.text:
Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

In this session, let us learn Computational Chemistry Introduction, Computational Methods and Applications.

Key details

  • Computational chemistry is a multidisciplinary area.
  • It involves maths, physics, and also chemistry basic information.
  • Computational chemistry is a branch of chemistry that uses mathematical algorithms, statistics, and computer simulations to study and solve chemical problems.
  • It does not directly replace experimental chemistry, but it complements predicting molecular structure, properties and reactions, explaining experimental observation.
  • reducing the cost and time of the experiment.
  • Computational chemistry refers to a collection of techniques used to investigate chemical problems with the aid of computers.
  • Rather than relying on laboratory experiments with chemicals, it applies the principles of theoretical chemistry through efficient computer program to predict and calculate molecular properties.
  • The earliest theoretical study was done in this field.
  • The experiment was carried out by Walter Hitler and Fritz Linden in 1927.
  • In the year nineteen ninety eight, Nobel Prize is awarded in chemistry to Walter Conn and John A Popel.
  • For the development of density functional theory, as well as for the contributions to the development of computational methods in quantum chemistry, which greatly advanced under practical applications of theoretical models.
  • In the year 2013, the Nobel Prize was awarded in chemistry for the development of computer based methods and simulate.
  • Complex chemical system enabling a deeper understanding of molecular process.
  • Objectives of computational chemistry.
  • It predicts and estimates the structure, stability, reactivity, and properties of molecules.
  • To provide reliable, accurate, and compressive information at anatomic level.
  • The advantages of computational chemistry are calculations are easy to perform than carrying out the experiments in the laboratory.
  • Calculations are less costly whereas experiments are becoming more expensive because not using any chemical molecule in the calculation process, so it is less costly.
  • Calculations are safer than performing the experiment in the lab.
  • These are the advantages of computational chemistry.
  • Scope of computational modeling.
  • The computational modeling can be used to accurately predict physical and chemical properties of molecule such as bond length, bond angles, humor and lumo interactions.
  • It can help in predicting the spectr of ultraviolet visible and IR spectroscopy, as well as proton nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
  • And also able to understand thermodynamic and kinetic properties.
  • According to thermodynamic properties are stable and unstable.
  • Whether the system is stable or unstable with respect to the chemistry molecule, whether the molecule is stable or highly unstable.
  • This can be determined thermodynamically.
  • Labelity means immediately it can undergo reaction.
  • Inertness means certain extent it is stable, higher the activation energy of the molecule.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

The electronic structure and all unmechanical properties can be determined by using computational modelling.

Key details

  • What we need to understand in the reaction, one can easily understand the activation energy.
  • After understanding the activation energy,.
  • At what temperature a reaction can be carried out?
  • What is the pressure?
  • Whether it requires to use the catalyst or not.
  • All these can be easily determined by using computational tool.
  • To know the underlying reaction mechanism and the kinetics of a reaction mechanism, computational chemistry plays a vital role in understanding.
  • What is the temperature, pressure, or catalyst is required or not to carry out the experiment in the laboratory.
  • And also it helps in material design.
  • In the by using computational modeling enables the rational design of new material with desired properties such as electrical conductivity, thermal stability, optical properties, magnetic properties.
  • and other properties can be designed easily with the help of computational tool.
  • This leads to the development of advanced material for energy production, storage application, especially in the batteries, capacitor, supercapacitor, electronics, and much more applications.
  • This is very, very important one in the pharmaceutical industry in the determination of drug.
  • Computational chemistry plays a pivotal role in design and the screening of potential drug candidates by simulating the interaction between the drug molecule and biological target, particularly in case of.
  • The cancer cells in a particular part of the DNA or an RNA molecule affected by cancer cells, where by using this computational model, one can easily discover a target molecule for the cancer cell.
  • develop in the human system.
  • That is why in the drug discovery computational model is very much useful, especially structure activity relationship of the drug molecule can be easily determined.
